title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 294
paragraphs: The customs they practise are inherited from their fathers, and they do not acquire others in addition; but besides other customs of theirs worthy of mention, they have one song, that of Linus — the same one who is sung of in Phoenicia, in Cyprus, and elsewhere, having however a name that differs according to the various nations. This song agrees exactly with what the Hellenes sing calling on the name of Linus; so that besides the many other things about which I wonder in matters concerning Egypt, I wonder especially about this — namely, where they got the song of Linus. It is clear, however, that they have sung this song from time immemorial; and in the Egyptian tongue Linus is called Maneros. The Egyptians told me that he was the only son of the man who first became king of Egypt, and that he died before his time and was honoured with these lamentations by the Egyptians; and that this was their first and only song.
